clue.text: Not one's first husband on board?

definitions.text: Not one's first husband on board?

parts.words: Not one's first husband on board?
parts.note: reads like a second marriage, but 'on board' points to a ship, where the officer below the captain's chief is the one meant

explanation.surface: A question about a remarriage, hinting the new husband is aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: On a merchant ship the officer ranking after the first officer is the next in line, the deputy's deputy.

clue.text: Aforementioned crew reportedly composed

indicators.note: reportedly means the clue words are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: aforementioned means said, and a rowing crew is an eight, so this is said-eight

explanation.surface: A news report describes the crew mentioned earlier as calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' signals that SAID EIGHT, spoken, gives the answer. An EIGHT is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Composed and sedate both describe someone calm and unflustered.

clue.text: Secret about to reach public

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
overt means open, done in public

explanation.surface: A hidden matter is about to be made known to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Covert operations are clandestine, kept hidden from view.

clue.text: Country air

parts.note: suggests fresh rural breezes, but read as the tune that belongs to a nation

explanation.definitionFit: Each nation has its own official song, an air sung at state occasions.

clue.text: Find Emile rambling in dangerous area

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so the letters of the two words wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to locate a man named Emile as he strolls through a perilous place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' rearranges the letters of FIND EMILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A field sown with explosive mines is a hazardous zone, also used figuratively for any risky subject.

clue.text: Carried part into Ted's domain

indicators.note: part says only a portion of the following words is wanted, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: Something was taken along into a man named Ted's territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' marks letters lying inside INTO TED'S; 'domain' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Toted is an informal past tense meaning lugged or hauled along.

clue.text: In favour of fellow university lecturer shortly

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone supports a colleague who teaches at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' belongs to the definition: the answer is a clipped form.
explanation.definitionFit: Prof is the informal clipping of professor, a senior academic teacher.

clue.text: About to include work, make progress on foot in long narrow shed

indicators.note: to include says the word for about takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: re means about, concerning
op is short for opus, a work
to walk is to move forward on foot

explanation.surface: Someone about to take on a job advances on foot through a long thin building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a spatial word, but it is RE; 'to include' is the containment signal, and OP for work is the crossword shortening of opus.
explanation.definitionFit: Rope was traditionally made by twisting strands along a very long covered alley built for that trade.

clue.text: They might transfer you to the other side

definitions.text: They might transfer you to the other side

parts.words: They might transfer you to the other side
parts.note: hints at death or a sports transfer, but means boatmen carrying passengers across water

explanation.definitionFit: Boatmen who carry passengers across a river or strait take them to the opposite bank.

clue.text: Counterpart on the other side has less feeling

parts.note: opposite means facing, on the other side
number means more numb, having less sensation

explanation.surface: Someone's equivalent across the table is less sensitive.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER is read as numb-er, 'more numb', not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Your equivalent in another team or organisation holds the matching role there.

clue.text: Going back to video, see chunk of turf on golf course

definitions.text: chunk of turf on golf course

indicators.note: Going back says the hidden letters are read backwards
see asks the solver to look into the two words just before it for a run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Rewinding a recording to look at a golfer's lump of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'see' in the definition, but 'see' marks the letters lying inside TO VIDEO; 'Going back' reads them backwards. The definition is the chunk of turf alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's club often gouges out a piece of grass and soil, which etiquette says should be replaced.

clue.text: On which a tenner is printed?

definitions.text: On which a tenner is printed?

parts.words: On which a tenner is printed?
parts.note: a ten-pound banknote is printed on special paper, but the clue means stationery for letters, a tenner being a note

explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is a ten-pound note, and writing paper for letters is the stationery a note goes on.

clue.text: Divert on smaller road

explanation.definitionFit: To divert is to switch something away; a side road branching off a main one is a smaller road.

clue.text: Ray Wood redesigned the space

indicators.note: redesigned means made over in a new form, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Ray Wood has remodelled a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' rearranges the letters of RAY WOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening in a wall filled by a door is a gap or space you pass through.

clue.text: Bird to leap about at said evening of song and dancing

parts.note: to caper is to skip and leap playfully

indicators.note: said signals that the word for a dance evening is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish social gathering with folk music and dancing

explanation.surface: A bird hops about at a Scottish dance party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' gives CAILLIE from CEILIDH spoken. A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish evening of folk dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The capercaillie is a large grouse of Scottish pine forests.

clue.text: Accelerator removed from Con's motor

indicators.note: removed is read as re-moved, moved again, so the letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, keeping the letters CONS

explanation.surface: Some device has been taken out of a man named Con's car engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' rearranges CONS MOTOR. A cosmotron is an early particle accelerator.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cosmotron was a particle accelerator built at Brookhaven in the 1950s.

clue.text: Cockney has selected what has been classified

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the initial H, so the word has loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before the H is dropped
sorted means picked out, selected

explanation.surface: A Londoner has chosen what has been put into categories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney' drops the H, giving AS. Cockneys, East Londoners, famously drop initial Hs.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted goods have been sorted into kinds, grouped by type.

clue.text: Related to and concerning the Eastern Mediterranean

parts.note: re means concerning, on the subject of
the Levant is the old name for the lands of the eastern Mediterranean shore

explanation.surface: Something connected with the lands at the eastern end of the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pertinent is connected or applicable to the matter in hand.

clue.text: High-flying attendants

parts.note: high-flying suggests ambitious success, but literally means serving passengers in the air

explanation.definitionFit: Cabin crew who serve passengers on aircraft work, literally, at altitude.

clue.text: One who cannot settle

parts.note: might suggest a wanderer or debtor, but means a restless person who keeps moving about

explanation.definitionFit: A restless person who squirms and keeps shifting can never sit still.

clue.text: The way a youth declared

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth

explanation.surface: How a young man made an announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: TED is a Teddy boy, a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated means said or announced formally.

clue.text: To excel-difficult to prove

indicators.note: difficult letters are awkward ones, so the two words are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Something is hard to demonstrate when one tries to outshine.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to rise above or surpass others.

clue.text: Sound sheepish describing flowers

indicators.note: Sound tells the solver to hear the next word rather than read it

parts.note: read as like sheep, so herds of sheep, flocks

explanation.surface: Someone sounding embarrassed while talking about blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheepish' is not shy here: it means to do with sheep, so FLOCKS, which spoken gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlox are garden plants with clusters of brightly coloured blooms.

clue.text: One qualified to examine pupils

parts.note: suggests a schoolteacher or examiner, but pupils are the dark centres of the eyes

explanation.definitionFit: An eye doctor checks the black openings at the centre of the iris.

clue.text: One on the way earning commission?

definitions.text: One on the way earning commission?

parts.words: One on the way earning commission?
parts.note: anyone journeying is on the way, but one paid by commission while journeying is a sales representative

explanation.definitionFit: A commercial salesman travels a territory and is paid a percentage on sales made.

clue.text: Prejudiced person has to put energy into part

indicators.note: into says the word for energy goes inside the word for part

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece
go means energy, drive

explanation.surface: An intolerant person must inject vigour into a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to put' is a link phrase; 'energy' gives GO as in full of go, and 'into' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot is intolerant of those with differing opinions or backgrounds.

clue.text: Do the heartless become feeble-minded?

indicators.note: heartless means losing the central letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A question whether the cruel lose their wits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle H of THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dote originally meant to be weak in mind, as in dotage, old age with failing wits.

clue.text: Acquitted according to one extra revised abridged edition

indicators.note: revised means altered in a new version, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ED is the short form of edition

explanation.surface: Someone cleared according to a further updated short version of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exonerated is to be cleared of blame or a charge.
